chunks: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Kufi narrated from Mundhir ibn Muhammad ibn Qabus from Nasr ibn al-Sindi from Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Sufyan al-Mustariq from Thalaba ibn Maimun from Malik al-Juhani from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah; and Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Thalaba ibn Maimun from Malik al-Juhani from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said:

I came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and found him thoughtful, drawing lines in the earth. I said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, why do I see you thoughtful, drawing lines in the earth? Is it out of desire for it?' He said: 'No, by Allah, I have never desired it, nor the world at all. But I was contemplating the offspring who will be born from the back of the eleventh of my sons; he is the Mahdi, who will fill it with justice and equity, as it was filled with oppression and tyranny. There will be for him a perplexity and an occultation, in which some people will go astray and others will be guided.' I said: 'O my master, how long will this perplexity and occultation be?' He said: 'Six days, or six months, or six years.' I said: 'And will this matter indeed come to pass?' He said: 'Yes, just as he is created.' 'And how do you know this, O Asbagh? They are the best of this Ummah, along with the righteous of this Household.' I said: 'Then what will happen after that?' He said: 'Then Allah will do what He wills, for He has beginnings, wills, ends, and terminations.'

key_terms.الْحَيْرَة: Perplexity or confusion regarding the Imam's status
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيُّ: The Mahdi (the Guided One), a title for the twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the Mahdi's occultation and his role in filling the earth with justice?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through multiple chains in al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) early foreknowledge of the Mahdi’s occultation (*ghayba*) and the theological concept of *al-bada'* (divine change in decree), explaining the varying durations of perplexity. It underscores the continuity of divine guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt, affirming the Imams as the 'best of the Ummah' and linking the Mahdi’s mission to the Quranic promise of inheriting the earth. The mention of *al-bada'* serves to reconcile the apparent contradiction in the duration of the occultation, emphasizing God’s absolute sovereignty over time and destiny.
